body.text: A proper fraction has a numerator smaller than its denominator (3/4). An improper fraction has a numerator equal to or larger than its denominator (7/4), and can be rewritten as a mixed number — a whole number plus a proper fraction. Convert 7/4: 7 ÷ 4 = 1 remainder 3, so 7/4 = 1¾.

A fraction converts to a decimal by dividing the numerator by the denominator. 3/4 = 3 ÷ 4 = 0.75 — this stops after two decimal places, so it is a terminating decimal. But 1/3 = 0.333... never stops; the 3 repeats forever, so it is a recurring decimal, usually written 0.3̇.

A percentage is a fraction out of 100. To turn a decimal into a percentage, multiply by 100: 0.75 x 100 = 75%. To turn a percentage into a decimal, divide by 100: 75% = 0.75. A fraction converts to a percentage the same way it converts to a decimal, then multiplied by 100.

To find a percentage of a quantity, convert the percentage to a decimal and multiply. A trader in Kampala sells a shirt marked at UGX 40 000 with a 15% discount. The discount is 15% of 40 000 = 0.15 x 40 000 = UGX 6 000, so the shirt sells for 40 000 - 6 000 = UGX 34 000.
